chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a shirt in which a man sweats while he is in a state of janabah until the shirt becomes wet. He said: “There is no harm in it, and if he wishes to sprinkle it with water, then let him do so.”

key_terms.الْقَمِيصِ: the shirt or garment being asked about
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem or objection legally
key_terms.يَعْرَقُ: he sweats, causing moisture on the garment

ai.seo_question: Does the sweat of a person in janabah make clothing impure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that sweat from a person in a state of janabah does not render the shirt impure. It also indicates that sprinkling the garment with water is permissible if one prefers, but it is not required.
